clue.text: Topping having that distinguished decoration

parts.note: taken as written
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order awarded for distinguished service

explanation.surface: Someone's hat or cake topping bears a medal of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: A thatch is the straw topping of a cottage roof; CH (Companion of Honour) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof covering of straw or reed sits on top of a cottage, so it is literally its topping.

clue.text: Joiner employed for a shed I've designed

indicators.note: designed here means newly arranged, so the letters of the phrase before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Glue was bought to build a garden shed someone has planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter working on the shed, but it is the definition: anything that joins. 'designed' rearranges A SHED I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue is a substance that sticks two things together, so it acts as a joiner.

clue.text: Girlfriend Strauss might have found down under

definitions.text: Girlfriend Strauss might have found down under

parts.words: Girlfriend Strauss might have found down under
parts.note: Strauss wrote waltzes, so a girl he met in Australia might be seen dancing one with him; the title is the Australian bush song

explanation.surface: The composer Strauss meeting a girlfriend on a trip to Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Johann Strauss was the waltz king; the answer is Australia's best-known folk song, read as a girl named Matilda being waltzed.
explanation.definitionFit: The bush ballad title can be read as a girl being danced around in three-four time, which suits a waltz composer in Australia.

clue.text: Sensitivity upsetting gravity really

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over and disordering, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity in physics
taken as written

explanation.surface: An upset caused by something that is serious, really.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' rearranges G (gravity's symbol) with REALLY. The whole word GRAVITY has seven letters but is the wrong ones.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy is the body's oversensitivity to a substance such as pollen.

clue.text: Offered this, who could ask for more?

definitions.text: Offered this, who could ask for more?

parts.words: Offered this, who could ask for more?
parts.note: a host's offer of unlimited helpings leaves nothing further to request

explanation.surface: Someone is offered so generously that no more could be asked.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer of unlimited quantity covers every possible wish, so asking for extra makes no sense.

clue.text: Part of speech unknown in 1 BC?

definitions.text: Part of speech unknown in 1 BC?

parts.words: Part of speech unknown in 1 BC?
parts.note: the Latin dating label Anno Domini was not yet in use before the first year of the Christian era, so a word built on it could not have existed

explanation.surface: A question about which grammatical term people did not know in ancient times.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as AD plus VERB: AD dating starts at year 1, so in 1 BC nobody had heard of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A word class that modifies verbs or adjectives, such as 'quickly', is one of the parts of speech.

clue.text: Drink that causes a stir right away

indicators.note: away means sent off, so the letter for right is removed

parts.note: taken as written, the two words run together; that they also start with the answer is a coincidence, since the clue's device is the removal of R

explanation.surface: A beverage that causes immediate excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' takes R (right) out of A STIR, leaving the Italian wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont, so it is a type of beverage.

clue.text: State a number of Romans held

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
held means possessed, which is had

explanation.surface: A country where Roman citizens were once held captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' looks like a container indicator, but it simply means HAD, placed after C (100 in Roman numerals).
explanation.definitionFit: Chad is a landlocked country in north-central Africa, so it is a nation state.

clue.text: Bore — and that's saying everything

indicators.note: saying means spoken out, so the word for everything is heard rather than read

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: A tedious person who insists on saying everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' reads as a dull person, but it is a verb: an awl bores holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool with a pointed spike makes holes in leather or wood, so it is used to bore.

clue.text: Wretched doctrine inflicting pain on others

definitions.note: a phrase describing the practice, defining the noun for it

parts.note: wretched means unhappy, sad
an ism is a doctrine or belief system

explanation.surface: A miserable creed that hurts other people.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadism is taking pleasure in causing cruelty and suffering to other people.

clue.text: One-way Somerset town, apparently

parts.note: a road with traffic in one direction takes its name from a small town in south-west England

explanation.surface: A small Somerset town that seems to have only one road through it.
explanation.walkthrough: Street is a town in Somerset, a county in south-west England; a one-way street restricts traffic to one direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The English town's name is also the common word for a road, as in a one-way road through town.

clue.text: French spirit on tap?

parts.note: the French brandy name means water of life, and water is what comes out of a tap

explanation.surface: A French liqueur served from a draught tap in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tap' suggests draught drink, but the point is that the first word of the French name means water, which comes out of the tap.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau-de-vie is French fruit brandy, a strong spirit whose name literally means water of life.

clue.text: One up for Shakespeare at an Eisteddfod ceremony?

definitions.text: One up for Shakespeare at an Eisteddfod ceremony?

parts.words: One up for Shakespeare at an Eisteddfod ceremony?
parts.note: at the Welsh festival the winning poet is ceremonially seated, and Shakespeare was the Bard of Avon

explanation.surface: Shakespeare is honoured at a Welsh cultural festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eisteddfod is a Welsh festival of poetry and music whose winning poet is seated in a carved chair; 'one up' suggests a score point but means raising someone in a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh rite of seating the winning poet in a special seat names the event.

clue.text: Feel remorse way across the Channel

definitions.meaning: the French word for a street, a way in France, across the English Channel

explanation.definitionFit: The English verb means regret, and the French noun means a city road.

clue.text: Roughly one gram for Napoleon's battle-charger

indicators.note: roughly suggests a rough approximate form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: About one gram of feed for Napoleon's warhorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' looks like an estimate of weight, but it rearranges ONE GRAM. Marengo was the horse named after Napoleon's 1800 victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Marengo was the grey Arab stallion Napoleon rode into battle, so it was his warhorse.

clue.text: Royal burgh on a short-time basis

parts.note: yr is the short form of year, a period of time

explanation.surface: A Scottish royal town used only temporarily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a ... basis' are link words; A plus YR, the abbreviation of year. Ayr is a Scottish town; a royal burgh is a Scottish town with a royal charter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a Scottish town granted a royal charter, the Scottish status of a chartered borough.

clue.text: David's book of pepper and salt? Go away!

annotationWithheld.why: David's book of pepper and salt? Go away! (7): P + SALT + ER is the apparent pattern, but no reading gives P from pepper and ER from 'Go away!' with each word doing one job
annotationWithheld.clue: David's book of pepper and salt? Go away!

clue.text: Plant adding stimulus to a bit of mischief?

parts.note: a lark is a prank, a bit of mischief
a spur is an incentive or stimulus

explanation.surface: Encouraging a small prank by adding an incentive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be a verb, to set or hide something, but here it is the noun: a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden flower, the delphinium, so it is a type of plant.

clue.text: Talked about an urban centre of Washington

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for talked goes around the next piece

parts.note: talked means spoke

explanation.surface: People discussed a city in the US capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington' suggests the US capital, but it is the state in the Pacific Northwest, where this is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Spokane is a large city in eastern Washington State, so it is one of its urban centres.

clue.text: Movement by degrees when one is getting on

definitions.text: Movement by degrees when one is getting on

parts.words: Movement by degrees when one is getting on
parts.note: advancing step by step, as someone does who is getting on, which is also making headway or growing older

explanation.surface: Slow advance as a person ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on' means both making headway and growing old; 'by degrees' means a little at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow, step-by-step advancement describes steady movement forward over time.

clue.text: Evidently one who doesn't repel advances

definitions.text: Evidently one who doesn't repel advances

parts.words: Evidently one who doesn't repel advances
parts.note: advances here are loans of money, and someone who accepts them owes money

explanation.surface: A person who welcomes romantic approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advances' suggests romantic overtures, but means loans; someone who accepts them ends up owing.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has accepted loans owes the lender money.

clue.text: Industrious yet sad somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are reworked into new order

explanation.surface: A hard-working person who is nonetheless unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges YET SAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady here means diligent and reliable, as a hard worker is.

clue.text: Ruddy good fellow, university type

parts.note: ruddy means reddish, red
a brick is a dated British term for a dependable, good person

explanation.surface: A rosy-faced decent chap of a certain academic kind.
explanation.walkthrough: A redbrick is one of the British universities founded in the industrial cities in the late 1800s, as opposed to Oxford and Cambridge; 'a brick' is old British slang for a good sort.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a type of British university built in Victorian industrial cities from red brick.

clue.text: She pined for Narcissus, it is recalled

definitions.text: She pined for Narcissus, it is recalled

parts.words: She pined for Narcissus, it is recalled
parts.note: the Greek nymph who loved the self-adoring youth wasted away until only her voice remained, repeating what others said

explanation.surface: A story recalling a woman who longed for Narcissus.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the nymph who loved Narcissus faded to a voice; 'recalled' also means called back, as a repeated sound is.
explanation.definitionFit: The nymph of myth gave her name to the repeated sound reflected back from a surface.

clue.text: Was Mr Heath so impaired?

parts.note: Ted Heath was the nickname of Edward Heath, British prime minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: A question whether a former prime minister was in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath, Conservative British prime minister 1970-74, was widely known as Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wasted has been weakened or spoiled, so it is damaged.

clue.text: Drove fowls away and lost two ducks in the process

indicators.note: the ducks are placed inside the word for lost as part of the procedure

parts.note: to shed is to lose, as a tree loses leaves
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, and O looks like zero, so two of them make OO

explanation.surface: A farmer chased the hens off and lost a couple of ducks doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' read as birds beside the fowls, but a duck is a nil score in cricket, the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoo birds is to drive them off with a cry and wave of the arms.

clue.text: A religious palindrome

indicators.note: the word reads the same in both directions, which is all the wordplay offers

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A holy woman whose name reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious, used as a noun, is a member of a religious order, as a sister in a convent is.

clue.text: Eastern tongue part of our duty to learn

indicators.note: part of means a piece taken from the words that follow, so the letters lie within them

explanation.surface: Learning a language as part of one's obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also spoken widely in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is a South Asian language, so from a Western viewpoint it is an Eastern tongue.
